question: In the Indian constitution, which original duties were added by the Act?  (RPF SI 2018 (11/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: 44th Amendment
41st Amendment
42nd  Amendment
52st  Amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 42nd Amendment

Explanation:
The Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976. This amendment was based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. It inserted Article 51A under Part IV-A of the Constitution, which lists 11 fundamental duties for citizens. These duties reflect moral and legal obligations. The 42nd Amendment was the most comprehensive amendment to the Indian Constitution and is often called the 'Mini-Constitution'. The other options: 44th Amendment (changed emergency provisions), 41st Amendment (governor's tenure), and 52nd Amendment (anti-defection law) are unrelated to Fundamental Duties.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which amendment added Fundamental Duties? → 42nd Amendment (1976)
☛ Which article contains Fundamental Duties? → Article 51A
☛ Which part contains Fundamental Duties? → Part IV-A
☛ Which committee recommended Fundamental Duties? → Swaran Singh Committee
☛ What is the 42nd Amendment also known as? → Mini-Constitution
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान में अधिनियम द्वारा कौन से मूल कर्तव्य जोड़े गए? (RPF SI 2018 (11/01/2019) Shift 2)
options_hi: 44वां संशोधन
41वां संशोधन
42वां संशोधन
52वां संशोधन
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है 42वां संशोधन

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान में मूल कर्तव्य (Fundamental Duties) को 42वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1976 द्वारा जोड़ा गया। यह संशोधन स्वर्ण सिंह समिति की सिफारिशों पर आधारित था। इस अधिनियम ने संविधान के भाग IV-A में अनुच्छेद 51A जोड़ा, जिसमें नागरिकों के लिए 11 मूल कर्तव्य निर्धारित किए गए। ये कर्तव्य नैतिक और कानूनी दायित्वों को दर्शाते हैं। 42वां संशोधन भारतीय संविधान का सबसे व्यापक संशोधन था, जिसे 'मिनी-कॉन्स्टिट्यूशन' भी कहा जाता है। अन्य विकल्पों में 44वां संशोधन (आपातकालीन प्रावधानों में बदलाव), 41वां (राज्यपालों का कार्यकाल) और 52वां (दलबदल विरोधी कानून) से संबंधित हैं।

question: How many ministers can be included in the Central Council of Ministers? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (31/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Fifty percent of the total members of the Lok Sabha
Fifteen percent of the total members of the Lok Sabha
Ten to fifteen percent of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
As desired by the Prime Minister of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Fifteen percent of the total members of the Lok Sabha

Explanation:
According to Article 75(1) of the Indian Constitution, the total number of ministers in the Central Council of Ministers shall not exceed 15% of the total members of the Lok Sabha. This provision was added by the 91st Constitutional Amendment (2003) to limit the size of the Council of Ministers and ensure efficiency. The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 552 (530 from states, 20 from union territories, and 2 nominated Anglo-Indians). Thus, the maximum number of ministers is about 83. This rule prevents the government from becoming too large and unwieldy.

question_hi: केंद्र की मंत्रिपरिषद में कितने मंत्रियों को सम्मिलित किया जा सकता है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (31/01/2021) Shift 1)
options_hi: लोक सभा के कुल सदस्यों के पचास प्रतिशत
लोक सभा के कुल सदस्यों के पंद्रह प्रतिशत
लोक सभा के सदस्यों की कुल संख्या के दस से पंद्रह प्रतिशत
भारत के प्रधानमंत्री की इच्छानुसार
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है लोक सभा के कुल सदस्यों के पंद्रह प्रतिशत

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 75(1) के अनुसार, केंद्रीय मंत्रिपरिषद में मंत्रियों की कुल संख्या लोक सभा के कुल सदस्यों के 15% से अधिक नहीं हो सकती। यह प्रावधान 91वें संविधान संशोधन (2003) द्वारा जोड़ा गया था ताकि मंत्रिपरिषद का आकार सीमित रहे और कार्यकुशलता बनी रहे। वर्तमान में लोक सभा की अधिकतम सदस्य संख्या 552 है, जिसमें 530 सीटें राज्यों से, 20 केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों से और 2 एंग्लो-इंडियन समुदाय से मनोनीत होती हैं। इसलिए मंत्रियों की अधिकतम संख्या 552 का 15% यानी लगभग 83 हो सकती है। यह नियम सरकार के आकार को नियंत्रित करता है और अनावश्यक विस्तार को रोकता है।

question: In which Constitutional Amendment Act were the seats of Lok Sabha increased from 525 to 545? (RRB JE CBT I (01/06/2019) Shift 1)
options: 25th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971
21st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1967
31st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1973
24th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 31st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1973

Explanation:
The 31st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1973 increased the number of Lok Sabha seats from 525 to 545. This amendment raised the representation of states from 525 to 543, and allowed the President to nominate 2 members from the Anglo-Indian community. Prior to this, the Lok Sabha had 499 seats in 1952, which later increased to 525. The 31st Amendment redistributed seats among states based on the 1971 Census, resulting in additional seats for some states. Currently, the maximum strength of Lok Sabha is 550 (543 elected + 2 nominated), which has been frozen until 2026 by the 84th Amendment. This amendment was significant in adjusting representation according to population growth.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which amendment increased Lok Sabha seats from 525 to 545? → 31st Constitutional Amendment, 1973
☛ Which amendment introduced nominated Anglo-Indian members in Lok Sabha? → 31st Constitutional Amendment, 1973
☛ How many elected seats were in Lok Sabha after the 31st Amendment? → 543
☛ Which amendments fixed the maximum Lok Sabha strength at 543+2? → 31st Amendment (1973) and 84th Amendment (2001)
☛ On which census is the current distribution of Lok Sabha seats based? → 1971 Census
question_hi: किस संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम द्वारा, लोकसभा की सीटों की संख्या 525 से बढ़ाकर 545 की गई ? (RRB JE CBT I (01/06/2019) Shift 1)

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है 31वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1973

Explanation:
31वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1973 द्वारा लोकसभा की सीटों की संख्या 525 से बढ़ाकर 545 की गई। इस संशोधन के तहत, लोकसभा में राज्यों का प्रतिनिधित्व 525 से बढ़ाकर 543 कर दिया गया और 2 सीटें एंग्लो-इंडियन समुदाय के लिए राष्ट्रपति द्वारा मनोनीत की जाने लगीं। इससे पहले, 1952 के लोकसभा चुनाव में 499 सीटें थीं, जो बाद में 525 हुईं। 31वें संशोधन के परिणामस्वरूप, विभिन्न राज्यों की जनसंख्या में वृद्धि के अनुपात में सीटों का पुनर्वितरण किया गया। यह संशोधन 1971 की जनगणना के आधार पर किया गया था, जिससे कुछ राज्यों को अतिरिक्त सीटें मिलीं। वर्तमान में लोकसभा की अधिकतम सीटें 550 (543 निर्वाचित + 2 मनोनीत) हैं, जो 84वें संशोधन द्वारा 2026 तक स्थिर रखी गई हैं।

question: Who among the following can propose a Government Bill? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Member of the Treasury Bench in Lok Sabha
A Member of Parliament who is not a Minister
Minister in either House of Parliament
Minister in Lok Sabha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Minister in either House of Parliament

Explanation:
A Government Bill is a bill introduced by a Minister. According to the Indian Constitution, any Minister, whether a member of the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha, can propose a Government Bill. It is important to note that only Ministers can introduce such bills, not ordinary Members of Parliament. The option 'Member of the Treasury Bench in Lok Sabha' also refers to Ministers, but it is limited to the Lok Sabha, whereas a Minister in either House can propose a bill. Hence, the correct answer is 'Minister in either House of Parliament'.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Who introduces a Private Member's Bill? → Ordinary MP (not a Minister)
☛ Who can propose a Money Bill? → Only a Minister in Lok Sabha
☛ Can a Government Bill be introduced in Rajya Sabha? → Yes, by a Minister
☛ Which Articles deal with bills in the Constitution? → Articles 107-111
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सरकारी विधेयक को प्रस्तावित कर सकता है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/02/2021) Shift 2)

संसद के किसी भी सदन में मंत्री

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है संसद के किसी भी सदन में मंत्री

Explanation:
सरकारी विधेयक (Government Bill) वह विधेयक है जो किसी मंत्री द्वारा प्रस्तुत किया जाता है। भारतीय संविधान के अनुसार, कोई भी मंत्री, चाहे वह लोकसभा का सदस्य हो या राज्यसभा का, सरकारी विधेयक प्रस्तावित कर सकता है। यह ध्यान रखना महत्वपूर्ण है कि सरकारी विधेयक केवल मंत्री ही पेश कर सकते हैं, न कि कोई सामान्य सांसद। ट्रेज़री बेंच के सदस्य भी मंत्री होते हैं, लेकिन यह विकल्प केवल लोकसभा तक सीमित है, जबकि मंत्री किसी भी सदन में विधेयक प्रस्तुत कर सकते हैं।

question: Who among the following was honoured with Bharat Ratna award before becoming the President of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Rajendra Prasad
S Radhakrishnan
VV Giri
pranab mukherjee
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is S Radhakrishnan

Explanation:
Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1954, India's highest civilian award. He served as the President of India from 1962 to 1967. Before becoming President, he was the Vice President of India (1952-1962). He was a renowned philosopher and educator. Rajendra Prasad received the Bharat Ratna in 1962, but he had already served as President (1950-1962). V.V. Giri and Pranab Mukherjee received this award after their presidencies.

question_hi: भारत के राष्ट्रपति बनने से पहले इनमें से किसे भारत रत्न पुरस्कार से सम्मानित किया गया था? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/02/2021) Shift 2)

Explanation:

question: Which of the following Constitution Amendments empowers Parliament to establish common High court for two or more than two States? (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (16/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: 6th Constitutional Amendment Act
8th Constitutional Amendment Act
7th Constitutional Amendment Act
9th Constitutional Amendment Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 7th Constitutional Amendment Act

Explanation:
The 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956 was enacted after the reorganisation of states. This amendment empowered Parliament to establish a common High Court for two or more states. Prior to this, each state had its own separate High Court. It inserted Article 231 into the Constitution, which allows the creation of a common High Court. For instance, the Punjab and Haryana High Court serves as a common High Court for both states. The 7th Amendment aligned with the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 and simplified judicial administration. It also amended the First and Fourth Schedules to accommodate the new state boundaries.

☛ How many schedules were amended by the 7th Amendment? → First and Fourth Schedules

☛ Example of a common High Court? → Punjab and Haryana High Court

solution:

Explanation:
In the 1993 case of Unni Krishnan vs State of Andhra Pradesh, the Supreme Court held that the fundamental right to primary education is part of the Right to Life under Article 21. This judgment paved the way for the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, which made education a fundamental right under Article 21A. question: Which of the following is related to Article 84 of the Constitution? (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (16/12/2024) Shift 3)

solution:

Explanation:
Article 84 of the Indian Constitution, under Part V, lays down the qualifications for becoming a member of Parliament. It requires a person to be a citizen of India, must have completed 25 years of age for Lok Sabha and 30 years for Rajya Sabha, and must possess other qualifications as prescribed by Parliament. This article is crucial for understanding the eligibility criteria for MPs. In contrast, Article 102 deals with disqualification of members, Article 112 with the Annual Financial Statement (Budget), and Article 123 with the President's ordinance-making power. question: Which of the following rights is NOT part of the Right to Life under Article 21 of the Indian Constitution?  (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (17/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: Right to Privacy
Right to Free Legal Aid
Right to Property
Right to Livelihood
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Right to Property

Explanation:
Article 21 of the Indian Constitution protects Right to Life and Personal Liberty. The Supreme Court has given it a wide interpretation, encompassing many rights such as Right to Privacy, Right to Free Legal Aid, Right to Livelihood, Right to a Clean Environment, Right to Live with Dignity, etc. However, the Right to Property was originally a fundamental right under Article 31 but was removed by the 44th Amendment (1978) and is now a legal right under Article 300A. Hence, the Right to Property is not part of the Right to Life under Article 21.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a Legislative Assembly for the National Capital Territory and the seats in such Assembly shall be filled by members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the National Capital Territory? (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (17/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: Article 239 B
Article 239 AA
Article 239 AB
Article 239A
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 239 AA

Explanation:
Article 239 AA of the Indian Constitution provides for a Legislative Assembly for the National Capital Territory of Delhi. According to this article, the seats in the Assembly are filled by members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies within the National Capital Territory. This article was inserted by the 69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991. Article 239 AA grants Delhi a special status, allowing it to have an elected government and a Council of Ministers, with the Lieutenant Governor as the administrator. It empowers the Assembly to make laws on matters in the State List and Concurrent List, except for public order, police, and land. Other options like Article 239 A, 239 AB, and 239 B are not related to this provision.

question: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court of India enunciate the ‘Doctrine of Basic Structure’? (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (17/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Golaknath case
AK Gopalan case
Menka Gandhi case
Keshvanand Bharti case
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Keshvanand Bharti case

Explanation:
The Supreme Court of India enunciated the Doctrine of Basic Structure in the Keshvanand Bharti case in 1973. According to this doctrine, Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot destroy or alter its basic structure. This landmark judgment limited Parliament's amending power and strengthened judicial review. The basic structure includes the supremacy of the Constitution, democratic and republican form of government, federal structure, separation of powers, and fundamental rights. In the Golaknath case (1967), the Court had held that Parliament cannot amend fundamental rights, but Keshvanand Bharti went further to establish the basic structure doctrine. This case is a cornerstone of Indian constitutional law.

☛ Menka Gandhi case (1978) → Interpretation of procedure under Article 21.
☛ AK Gopalan case (1950) → Narrow interpretation of Article 21.
☛ Basic Structure includes: Supremacy of Constitution, Democracy, Republic, Federalism, Separation of Powers.

question: The Indian Constitution guarantees Fundamental Rights to its citizens under which of the following Articles? (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (17/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Only Articles 12 to 35
Only Articles 14 to 32
Only Articles 12 to 30
Only Articles 15 to 35
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Only Articles 12 to 35

Explanation:
Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution, which spans from Article 12 to Article 35. Article 12 defines the term 'State', Article 13 deals with the doctrine of judicial review of laws, and Articles 14 to 32 enumerate specific rights such as right to equality, freedom, protection against exploitation, religious freedom, cultural education, and constitutional remedies. Articles 33 to 35 contain special provisions like restrictions on rights for armed forces, martial law, and enforcement of rights. Therefore, the entire spectrum of Fundamental Rights is covered under Articles 12 to 35.

question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act is known as the 'Right to Education' Amendment? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 1)

101st Amendment
solution:

question: The Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution have a resemblance to which of the following international declarations? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: United Nations Charter
Geneva Convention
International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights
Universal Declaration of Human Rights
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Universal Declaration of Human Rights

Explanation:
The Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. These duties are inspired by the spirit of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR), which also emphasizes citizens' responsibilities alongside rights. Article 29 of the UDHR states that everyone has duties to the community. The Indian Constitution originally listed 10 Fundamental Duties; the 11th was added by the 86th Amendment (2002). It is important to note that these duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by courts. The concept of duties was also influenced by the Constitution of the former Soviet Union.

question: Dr. BR Ambedkar described which part of the Indian Constitution as its ‘novel features', while Granville Austin referred to it as the ‘Conscience of the Constitution’? (RRB JE ECE (22/04/2025) Shift 1 CBT 2)
options: Directive Principles of State Policy
Fundamental Rights
Preamble
Fundamental Duties
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Directive Principles of State Policy

Explanation:
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described the Directive Principles of State Policy as the 'novel features' of the Constitution because they are a unique and fundamental characteristic of the Indian Constitution. These principles are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Constitution. Granville Austin called them the 'Conscience of the Constitution' as they guide the state towards achieving socio-economic justice. These principles are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country. They are inspired by the Irish Constitution and are based on the concept of a welfare state. They aim to establish social and economic democracy in India.

question: The Supreme Court can issue writs under Article 32 only for which specific purpose? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: To protect Fundamental Rights
To review decisions of statutory tribunals
To enforce the Directive Principles of State Policy
To resolve disputes between states
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To protect Fundamental Rights

Explanation:
Article 32 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. It is itself a Fundamental Right. Under this article, the Supreme Court can issue five types of writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto. These writs can be issued only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights, not for other legal or constitutional purposes. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution. This provision ensures that citizens have a constitutional remedy when their Fundamental Rights are violated.

solution_hi:

question: Which criticism highlights the parliamentary system’s departure from the principle of separation of powers? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: The President has absolute control over the Prime Minister.
The cabinet simultaneously leads the executive and legislature, creating fusion of powers.
The executive and legislature operate independently.
Ministers are appointed based on expertise rather than political affiliation.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The cabinet simultaneously leads the executive and legislature, creating fusion of powers.

Explanation:
In a parliamentary system, there is a fusion of powers rather than a separation of powers. The cabinet leads both the executive (government) and the legislature (parliament), as ministers are themselves members of the legislature. This departure from the principle of separation of powers is criticized because it concentrates too much power and weakens checks and balances. Other options are incorrect: the President does not have absolute control over the Prime Minister; the executive and legislature are not independent; ministers are appointed based on political affiliation, not expertise.

question_hi: संसदीय प्रणाली के शक्तियों के पृथक्करण के सिद्धांत से विचलन पर कौन सी आलोचना प्रकाश डालती है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: राष्ट्रपति को प्रधानमंत्री पर पूर्ण नियंत्रण है।
मंत्रिमंडल एक साथ कार्यपालिका और विधायिका का नेतृत्व करता है, जिससे शक्तियों का सम्मिश्रण होता है।
कार्यपालिका और विधायिका स्वतंत्र रूप से कार्य करते हैं।
मंत्रियों की नियुक्ति राजनीतिक संबद्धता के बजाय विशेषज्ञता के आधार पर की जाती है।
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है मंत्रिमंडल एक साथ कार्यपालिका और विधायिका का नेतृत्व करता है, जिससे शक्तियों का सम्मिश्रण होता है।

Explanation:
संसदीय प्रणाली में शक्तियों का पृथक्करण नहीं होता, बल्कि शक्तियों का सम्मिश्रण होता है। मंत्रिमंडल कार्यपालिका (सरकार) और विधायिका (संसद) दोनों का नेतृत्व करता है, क्योंकि मंत्री स्वयं संसद के सदस्य होते हैं। यह संरचना शक्तियों के पृथक्करण के सिद्धांत से विचलन है, जिसकी आलोचना की जाती है कि इससे शक्तियों का अत्यधिक केंद्रीकरण होता है और नियंत्रण संतुलन कमजोर होता है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं: राष्ट्रपति का प्रधानमंत्री पर पूर्ण नियंत्रण नहीं होता; कार्यपालिका और विधायिका स्वतंत्र नहीं होते; मंत्रियों की नियुक्ति राजनीतिक आधार पर होती है।
